d: Provide O(1) average time complexity for lookups, insertions, and deletions.

p: Hash Maps (Dictionaries in Python) use a hashing function to map keys to buckets in an array. This provides an expected O(1) time complexity for insertions, deletions, and lookups, making it the most powerful data structure in coding interviews.
2. Use it to store frequencies (character counts) or seen values (Two Sum).
3. Check `if key in map` to achieve O(1) lookups instead of O(N) nested loops.

def twoSum(nums, target):
  prevMap = {} # val : index
  for i, n in enumerate(nums):
    diff = target - n
    if diff in prevMap:
      return [prevMap[diff], i]
    prevMap[n] = i
  return []
Time: O(N) total, O(1) per operation. Space: O(N) to store elements.

"Apple"  -> H() ->   [0] -> null
"Banana" -> H() ->   [1] -> "Banana"
"Mango"  -> H() ->   [2] -> "Apple" -> "Mango" (Collision!)
